newsitem.title: NIGERIA: West African leaders meet on Liberian poll date.
newsitem.headline: West African leaders meet on Liberian poll date.

text.p: Several West African heads of state are meeting in Nigeria's capital Abuja on Wednesday to fix a date for general elections expected to consolidate the end of seven years of civil war in Liberia.

Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi told state television that the date would be made known at the end of the one-day summit of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) committee of nine on Liberia.
Some of the heads of state, including those of Niger, Benin, Mali and Burkina Faso, arrived in Abuja on Tuesday while Togolese President Gnassingbe Eyadema sent his prime minister.
Officials said the heads of state of Ivory Coast, Senegal and Ghana were flying in on Wednesday morning in time for the talks due to start at about midday.

The presidential and legislative polls originally set for May 30 are likely to be held in July, according to Liberian leaders who have been meeting in Abuja for the past week to decide when to hold the elections.
They said proposals put forward by the independent electoral commission in Abuja and adopted by all the parties sought a delay of 50 days to allow for more preparations.

The Liberian leaders, including former warlords, tribal chiefs, politicians and representatives of the electoral commission, met Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha last Friday to decide when to hold the elections.
Abacha told them there was a limit to the sacrifice West Africa could continue to bear to bring peace in Liberia.
The May date was part of a peace plan brokered in Abuja last August by ECOWAS, of which Abacha is chairman, and backed by the Nigerian-led African peacekeeping force ECOMOG.
Most of the Liberian leaders have called for a postponement until August or September for security reasons, logistics and lack of voter education.
The ECOWAS committee of nine will also decide whether there should be separate ballots for the presidential and legislative elections or whether they should be held at the same time.
Freed American slaves founded Liberia in 1847. The war has killed more than 150,000 people and displaced half the pre-war population of 2.5 million.
Hundreds of thousands of Liberians are refugees in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone. Others are in Ghana and Nigeria.
